solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rescue vessel wrecked on a hot island

indicators.note: something wrecked is broken up, so the two letters of 'on' are rearranged

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
Sark is one of the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A lifeboat has run aground on a sweltering island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' looks like a description of the vessel, but it is the anagram signal. Sark is a small Channel Island between Guernsey and Jersey.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical boat saved Noah, his family and the animals from the Flood, a rescue on a grand scale.

clue.text: Aristocrat pens book revealing bribe

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the aristocrat word holds the book letter

parts.note: a noble is an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A lord writes a volume exposing corruption.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble is British slang for bribing or improperly influencing someone, such as a juror.

clue.text: Literary lion takes time on a slope

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia books

explanation.surface: A famous writer takes his time on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary lion' suggests a celebrated author, but it is a lion from a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at an angle or slantwise, so tilted like a slope.

clue.text: Star, not a person who could catch sole killer

indicators.note: not says the word star is used without the single letter that follows

parts.note: an angler is someone fishing, who might land a sole (a flatfish)

explanation.surface: A celebrity, not a fisherman, is the lone murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sole' looks like 'only', but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a murderer who chokes the victim.

clue.text: A CD, Sir Arthur Bliss's last works, inspiring second composer

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the jumble takes in the extra letter
works as a verb means is worked over, so these letters are rearranged
last means only the final letter of Bliss's is used

explanation.surface: A recording of the English composer Sir Arthur Bliss's final pieces stirs another composer.
explanation.definitionFit: The German composer wrote Also sprach Zarathustra and Der Rosenkavalier.

clue.text: Wrongdoing linked with a former war zone

parts.note: a crime is an act of wrongdoing

explanation.surface: Criminal activity is tied to a place once fought over.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula was the scene of the Crimean War in the 1850s, a battleground in history.

clue.text: Half-hearted scolder upset king's daughter

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards
the heart of the scolder word is a double letter; half-hearted keeps only one

parts.note: a nagger is someone who scolds

explanation.surface: A lukewarm nag annoyed a royal princess.
explanation.walkthrough: NAGGER loses one of its central Gs to give NAGER, which reversed gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Regan is one of King Lear's two treacherous daughters in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Losing two pounds, Malcolm worried about his virility

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the following word
worried means agitated, so the letters left are shaken into a new order
losing says the pound letters are taken out of the name

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two of them are LL

explanation.surface: Having lost weight, a man frets over his manhood.
explanation.walkthrough: MALCOLM minus two Ls leaves MACOM, rearranged by 'worried' to MACMO, which goes 'about' HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Machismo is aggressive masculine pride, a show of manliness.

clue.text: Totally grisly, gripping end to macabre tale

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the outer words clutch the extra letter

parts.note: all, as in all wrong, means totally
gory means grisly or bloody

indicators.note: end to means the final letter of macabre is taken

explanation.surface: A thoroughly gruesome, gripping horror story.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegory is a story whose characters and events carry a hidden moral or political meaning.

clue.text: Overworked retailer may be so disorganised

definitions.meaning: a harassed shopkeeper is busy in every part of the store
chaotic or scattered in every direction

explanation.surface: A frantic shopkeeper is likely to be in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: the retailer rushes everywhere in the store.
explanation.definitionFit: The British idiom means in a muddle or scattered everywhere.

clue.text: Blunt fatty shortened belt

parts.note: blunt, as in plain-spoken, can mean bald: a bald statement

indicators.note: shortened says the word for fatty loses its final letter

parts.note: rich food is fatty

explanation.surface: A frank remark about an overweight person's belt being taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a belt worn over one shoulder, slung across the body to carry a sword.

clue.text: Reasonable description of diet food impresses soldier

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so the soldier is set inside the food description

parts.note: diet food may be described as low-cal, written here as LOCAL
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A slimming product's label wins over a military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low-cal' (low in calories) is read as LOCAL, a common crossword trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Something logical follows sound reasoning, so it is sensible or rational.

clue.text: Revolutionary heading from Leicester Square returns

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, taken here from Leicester
returns means the number word is read backwards

parts.note: nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: A radical comes back from Leicester Square, the London West End plaza.
explanation.walkthrough: Leicester Square is a famous square in London's West End; here it splits into a letter source and a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Vladimir Lenin led the Bolshevik revolution in Russia in 1917.

clue.text: Rich adult forming relationships around university

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: around says the bonding word goes around the university letter

parts.note: bonding is forming close relationships

explanation.surface: A wealthy grown-up making friends on campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Abounding means plentiful or well supplied, as in a region rich in wildlife.

clue.text: Advantage having husband in prison? It strikes a heavy blow

indicators.note: in says the advantage and husband sit inside the prison word

parts.note: the slammer is slang for prison
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: Someone gains the upper hand with a spouse behind bars, then the clue pivots to a violent blow.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a heavy long-handled hammer used for breaking stone or driving stakes.

clue.text: A jackass brought up point, displaying hauteur

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a jackass is a fool
a ness is a headland or point, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A donkey raised to a point of looking haughty.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauteur is a haughty, distant manner, the same as standoffishness.

clue.text: A media broadcast covering California's scholarly world

indicators.note: covering says the jumbled letters wrap around the state abbreviation
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

explanation.surface: A TV and radio report on California's universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the community and environment of universities and research.

clue.text: Politician with minister to protect

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative politician
to minister to someone is to serve them

explanation.surface: An MP and a cleric team up to defend something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a noun but is the verb, as in 'minister to the sick'.
explanation.definitionFit: To conserve is to preserve and keep from harm or waste.

clue.text: Move corn or oat — tip for good farming practice?

indicators.note: move signals that the letters of the fodder are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Advice to a farmer: change where corn or oats are grown, a hint for sound agriculture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Move' is the anagram signal for CORN OR OAT plus TIP together.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers change which plant grows in each field from year to year to keep the soil healthy.

clue.text: Supply new equipment and thief turns up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the word is flipped to read upwards

parts.note: a looter is a thief

explanation.surface: A workshop is re-equipped and then a burglar arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: To retool is to fit a factory with fresh machinery and tools.

clue.text: D Washington's co-star in Philadelphia cheers

definitions.meaning: Tom Hanks co-starred with Denzel Washington in the 1993 film Philadelphia, giving T plus his surname
cheers is a British informal way of saying thank you

explanation.surface: A film actor's partner in a movie is applauded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Philadelphia' looks like the city, but it is the film; Tom Hanks is reduced to his initial plus surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers is British slang expressing gratitude, an informal word of appreciation.

clue.text: European character breaks engagement for show

indicators.note: breaks says the engagement word is split open to take the other letters

parts.note: a date is an engagement or appointment
a sign is a written character or symbol

explanation.surface: A continental figure interrupts a booking for a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: To designate is to indicate or point out, the verb sense of show.

clue.text: Class brainbox lacks ego

indicators.note: lacks says the word for brainbox is missing the ego letter

parts.note: a brainbox is British slang for a very clever person, a genius
I is the self, the ego

explanation.surface: A modest top student in the class.
explanation.definitionFit: In biology a genus is a classification rank grouping related species, so it is a class or kind.

clue.text: Meat that's raw changing hands

indicators.note: the hands are right and left, so the right-hand letter is swapped for the left-hand one

parts.note: fresh produce is raw or uncooked

explanation.surface: Uncooked meat passing from one owner to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Flesh is the soft tissue of an animal body, which as food is meat.

clue.text: More than one jolly complicated seminar

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so the word seminar is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful remark that a seminar was very intricate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' looks like 'very', but a Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine.
explanation.definitionFit: Jolly is a nickname for a sea soldier of the Royal Marines; the plural covers more than one.

clue.text: He would possess overwhelming love for dance

indicators.note: overwhelming suggests surrounding and swamping, so the love letter goes inside

parts.note: he would contracts to he'd, written HED
O is love, a zero score in tennis
to own is to possess

explanation.surface: A man would be swept up by passion for dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance or the social gathering where it is held.

clue.text: A kid is relaxed

parts.note: to kid someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: A young goat, or a child, is calm.
explanation.definitionFit: At ease is the military order to stand relaxed, and means comfortable generally.

clue.text: Advocates having porters perhaps outside station

indicators.note: outside says the beer word wraps around the station word

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ales
a post is a station, as a sentry's post

explanation.surface: Champions of a cause with railway baggage carriers outside the terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostles are passionate supporters or promoters of a cause, as well as the first disciples.
